issues.title: Wire `--target {claude,codex,all}` through capture-hooks install/uninstall/status
issues.impact: `iai-mcp capture-hooks install|status --target codex|all` exits with `error: unrecognized arguments: --target` because the subparser registers no such option; and where the option *is* added, the handlers (`cmd_capture_hooks_install`, `_uninstall`, `_status`) never read `args.target` and call path helpers that hard-code `~/.claude`. Net effect: Codex/all targeting is a no-op, and the documented commands in the install scripts fail outright.
issues.source: #2 (gemini `cli/__init__.py:561`; codex `cli/__init__.py:558`), #4 (codex `_capture.py:718`), #5 (codex `codex_install.sh:36`), #10 (codex `install_hosts.sh:117`); also surfaced in #3, #8, #11. This is the single highest-leverage fix - it clears comments across the Hooks, Packaging, and Docs PRs.
issues.body:
**Impact:** `iai-mcp capture-hooks install|status --target codex|all` exits with `error: unrecognized arguments: --target` because the subparser registers no such option; and where the option *is* added, the handlers (`cmd_capture_hooks_install`, `_uninstall`, `_status`) never read `args.target` and call path helpers that hard-code `~/.claude`. Net effect: Codex/all targeting is a no-op, and the documented commands in the install scripts fail outright.

**Affected:** `src/iai_mcp/cli/__init__.py` (capture-hooks subparser, ~L558-561), `src/iai_mcp/cli/_capture.py` (the three handlers, ~L718).

**Source (reviewers + PRs):** #2 (gemini `cli/__init__.py:561`; codex `cli/__init__.py:558`), #4 (codex `_capture.py:718`), #5 (codex `codex_install.sh:36`), #10 (codex `install_hosts.sh:117`); also surfaced in #3, #8, #11. This is the single highest-leverage fix - it clears comments across the Hooks, Packaging, and Docs PRs.

**PR links:** [#2](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/2) · [#3](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/3) · [#4](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/4) · [#5](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/5) · [#8](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/8) · [#10](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/10) · [#11](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/11)

issues.title: Codex capture installs Claude-format scripts; add a Codex rollout parser
issues.impact: For `--target codex`, the bundled `iai-mcp-turn-capture.sh` / `iai-mcp-session-capture.sh` parse Claude-style JSONL (top-level `type: user/assistant` or `message.role`, plus `~/.claude/projects` scanning). Current Codex rollout JSONL is `session_meta`/`response_item` records with the message under `payload`, and the Codex hook contract exposes `prompt` (UserPromptSubmit) and `last_assistant_message` (Stop). So every Codex conversation line is skipped - capture silently produces nothing. Hook templates also still hard-code `~/.claude/projects` for scan/fallback.
issues.affected: `src/iai_mcp/cli/_capture.py` (~L438, L540, L543), hook templates; Codex parsing path.
issues.source: #3 (codex `_capture.py:543`), #4 (codex `_capture.py:438`), #11 (codex `_capture.py:540`; gemini `_capture.py:330`). Closely related to I6 in Project 2 (same Codex format gap on the import path).

issues.title: Codex `Stop` hook uses the session-end script (turn-scoped -> duplicate re-emit)
issues.impact: `--target codex` registers `iai-mcp-session-capture.sh` as the Codex `Stop` hook. That script rolls over `.live.jsonl` and removes `{session_id}.offset` as if the session ended - but Codex `Stop` is turn-scoped and fires after every assistant turn. The next `UserPromptSubmit` then starts from offset 0 and re-emits earlier transcript lines, duplicating memories.

The next `UserPromptSubmit` then starts from offset 0 and re-emits earlier transcript lines, duplicating memories.

**Affected:** `src/iai_mcp/cli/_capture.py:539` (Codex Stop registration).

issues.title: `turn-capture.sh` stdin parsing: IFS tab-collapse + stale-transcript precedence (data corruption)
issues.impact: Two related bugs: (1) When `transcript_path` is empty but `hook_event_name` is present, the `read` with tab `IFS` collapses consecutive tabs, so `hook_event_name` (e.g. `UserPromptSubmit`) lands in `transcript_path`; if a file by that name exists in the cwd, `_is_usable()` accepts it and the session offset advances against the wrong file. (2) A non-empty but stale/foreign stdin `transcript_path` is accepted merely because it's readable, overriding the canonical `~/.claude/projects/*/{session_id}.jsonl` - so another session's turns get written under the current `session_id` and the deferred live file is corrupted.
issues.body:
**Impact:** Two related bugs: (1) When `transcript_path` is empty but `hook_event_name` is present, the `read` with tab `IFS` collapses consecutive tabs, so `hook_event_name` (e.g. `UserPromptSubmit`) lands in `transcript_path`; if a file by that name exists in the cwd, `_is_usable()` accepts it and the session offset advances against the wrong file. (2) A non-empty but stale/foreign stdin `transcript_path` is accepted merely because it's readable, overriding the canonical `~/.claude/projects/*/{session_id}.jsonl` - so another session's turns get written under the current `session_id` and the deferred live file is corrupted.

**Affected:** `src/iai_mcp/_deploy/hooks/iai-mcp-turn-capture.sh` (~L31 parsing, ~L86 usability/precedence).

**Source (reviewers + PRs):** #6 (gemini `:31`; codex `:86` and `:31`).

issues.title: Codex hook status over-reports ACTIVE
issues.impact: `capture-hooks status --target codex` returns ACTIVE/`0` based only on file + marker presence. It ignores that (a) Codex non-managed command hooks are skipped until the user trusts them via `/hooks`; (b) `[features].hooks = false` (or admin policy) disables hooks; (c) hooks defined via inline `[hooks]` in `config.toml` or a trusted project `.codex/hooks.json` exist but aren't read (reported NOT WIRED). So a fresh install looks healthy while nothing runs - and some valid setups look broken.

issues.title: Quote paths in generated Codex hook commands (spaces in home dir)
issues.impact: With a home directory containing whitespace, generated commands like `bash /Users/Jane Doe/.codex/hooks/...` are stored unquoted; Codex passes the string to the shell, which splits on the space, and `bash` tries to open only the first segment -> the hook silently never runs.
issues.body:
**Impact:** With a home directory containing whitespace, generated commands like `bash /Users/Jane Doe/.codex/hooks/...` are stored unquoted; Codex passes the string to the shell, which splits on the space, and `bash` tries to open only the first segment -> the hook silently never runs.

**Affected:** `src/iai_mcp/cli/_capture.py:451`.

**Source (reviewers + PRs):** #4 (codex `:451`).

**PR links:** [#4](https://github.com/gardinermichael/iai-personal-memory-engine/pull/4)

issues.title: Harden CLI path resolution / caching for hooks
issues.impact: (1) `sys.argv[0]` access can raise `IndexError` in embedded/test environments. (2) Caching the PATH entry into `~/.iai-mcp/.cli-path` instead of the currently-running executable can pin the installed hooks to a stale/wrong environment when a different `iai-mcp` is earlier on PATH. (3) The Codex session-recall script's CLI resolution checks only a few fixed locations and misses pipx/pyenv/Homebrew/venv installs (the Stop hook additionally does `command -v`).

issues.title: `check_capture_hooks.sh`: Codex coverage, per-host log scoping, macOS robustness
issues.impact: (a) An empty `PROBES` array under `set -u` throws "unbound variable" and crashes on macOS Bash 3.2. (b) `gtimeout` isn't supported and probes can run uncapped, so a CLI that blocks on startup hangs the health check despite the advertised 5s timeout. (c) It never inspects `~/.codex/hooks.json`, so a broken Codex hook reports SKIPPED/OK. (d) Shared `capture-*`/`turn-capture-*` logs let a never-run host falsely report OK. (e) A broad `hook`/`hooks` marker flags MCP-only configs as capture-configured. (Plus a redundant `print_log_summary` call.)
issues.affected: `scripts/check_capture_hooks.sh` (~L49, L50, L105, L107, L160, L195, L209).
issues.body:
**Impact:** (a) An empty `PROBES` array under `set -u` throws "unbound variable" and crashes on macOS Bash 3.2. (b) `gtimeout` isn't supported and probes can run uncapped, so a CLI that blocks on startup hangs the health check despite the advertised 5s timeout. (c) It never inspects `~/.codex/hooks.json`, so a broken Codex hook reports SKIPPED/OK. (d) Shared `capture-*`/`turn-capture-*` logs let a never-run host falsely report OK. (e) A broad `hook`/`hooks` marker flags MCP-only configs as capture-configured. (Plus a redundant `print_log_summary` call.)

issues.title: `codex_install.sh`: python3 preflight, UTF-8 I/O, TOML array-table boundary
issues.impact: No preflight that `python3` exists (script fails midway if absent); `read_text`/`write_text` use the locale default encoding (corruption risk on non-UTF-8 locales - pass `encoding="utf-8"`); and the `[features]` boundary scan doesn't recognize `[[hooks.X]]` double-bracket array tables, so `hooks = true` can be inserted into the wrong table. (The script also invokes the unsupported `--target` flag - see H1.)
issues.body:

(The script also invokes the unsupported `--target` flag - see H1.)

**Affected:** `scripts/codex_install.sh` (~L32, L59, L103, L80).

issues.title: `install_hosts.sh`: resolve venv Python/`iai-mcp` instead of bare PATH; catch `OSError`
issues.impact: The script calls bare `python3` / `iai-mcp` and depends on the user's PATH - which fails right after `install.sh` before the shell is restarted; it should resolve the venv interpreter/executable first and fall back to system. Config reads catch only `json.JSONDecodeError`, not `OSError`/`PermissionError`, so an unreadable config crashes the script.
issues.affected: `scripts/install_hosts.sh` (~L12, L31, L55, L72, L83, L121, L125).

_Triage ref: H11 · Project 1 (Capture Hooks (Claude + Codex)) · from the Outline PR-triage gameplan._

issues.title: `install_hosts.sh`: `--scope user`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, stale entries, TOML `[features]` comments
issues.impact: (a) Registers the Claude Code MCP at the default `local` scope, so the memory tools disappear in other projects - needs `--scope user`. (b) Always patches `~/.config/Claude`, ignoring `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. (c) Treats the mere presence of `[mcp_servers.iai-mcp]` as success and never refreshes stale `args`/env after a moved checkout, so Codex keeps launching a stale wrapper. (d) The `[features]` regex doesn't match a trailing comment (`[features] # ...`), so it appends a second `[features]` table and invalidates `config.toml`.
issues.body:
**Impact:** (a) Registers the Claude Code MCP at the default `local` scope, so the memory tools disappear in other projects - needs `--scope user`. (b) Always patches `~/.config/Claude`, ignoring `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. (c) Treats the mere presence of `[mcp_servers.iai-mcp]` as success and never refreshes stale `args`/env after a moved checkout, so Codex keeps launching a stale wrapper. (d) The `[features]` regex doesn't match a trailing comment (`[features] # ...`), so it appends a second `[features]` table and invalidates `config.toml`.

**Affected:** `scripts/install_hosts.sh` (~L23, L43, L83, L96).

**Source (reviewers + PRs):** #10 (codex `:23/:43/:83/:96`).

issues.title: Track per-target install success; skip post-install steps for failed targets
issues.impact: If a target's hook install fails (missing template, non-zero exit), the command still patches Claude configs and prints restart instructions for it. Track which targets succeeded and only run post-install config / print instructions for those. Also replace the subtle `ok = _install...(target) and ok` short-circuit pattern (used to force evaluation) with something less fragile.
issues.body:
**Impact:** If a target's hook install fails (missing template, non-zero exit), the command still patches Claude configs and prints restart instructions for it. Track which targets succeeded and only run post-install config / print instructions for those. Also replace the subtle `ok = _install...(target) and ok` short-circuit pattern (used to force evaluation) with something less fragile.

**Affected:** `src/iai_mcp/cli/_capture.py` (~L636, L625, L750).

**Source (reviewers + PRs):** #11 (gemini `:636`), #3 (gemini `:625/:750`).

issues.title: Python 3.11 f-string-backslash crash in `install_hosts.sh` heredoc
issues.impact: An embedded Python heredoc puts a backslash inside an f-string expression, which is a `SyntaxError` before Python 3.12. The project supports `>=3.11,<3.13`, so on 3.11 the Codex-setup heredoc fails to parse before doing any work.
issues.source: #10 (codex `:87`). Same Python-3.11 theme as C7 in Project 4.

issues.title: `import-sessions` module / arg wiring
issues.impact: #16 wires a lazy handler that imports `iai_mcp.cli._import_sessions`, but that module doesn't exist in the tree -> `ModuleNotFoundError` the moment you run `iai-mcp import-sessions`. In #30 the module exists, but `--target/--path/--dry-run/--max-turns` are defined identically on both the parent parser and the subparsers (redundant + desync-prone), and an option placed before the subcommand is overwritten by the child's default - e.g. `import-sessions --dry-run import` parses back to `dry_run=False`.
issues.body:
**Impact:** #16 wires a lazy handler that imports `iai_mcp.cli._import_sessions`, but that module doesn't exist in the tree -> `ModuleNotFoundError` the moment you run `iai-mcp import-sessions`. In #30 the module exists, but `--target/--path/--dry-run/--max-turns` are defined identically on both the parent parser and the subparsers (redundant + desync-prone), and an option placed before the subcommand is overwritten by the child's default - e.g. `import-sessions --dry-run import` parses back to `dry_run=False`.

**Affected:** `src/iai_mcp/cli/__init__.py` (~L402, L541, L575), `src/iai_mcp/cli/_import_sessions.py`.

issues.title: Close/flush `MemoryStore` in import paths (buffered writes lost = data loss)
issues.impact: `MemoryStore` buffers DB writes; if `store.close()` isn't called, the last batch's buffered items never hit the database. The import reports success while silently dropping records. Wrap the store in a context manager (or `close()` in a `finally`) before reporting success.
issues.body:
**Impact:** `MemoryStore` buffers DB writes; if `store.close()` isn't called, the last batch's buffered items never hit the database. The import reports success while silently dropping records. Wrap the store in a context manager (or `close()` in a `finally`) before reporting success.

**Affected:** `src/iai_mcp/cli/_capture.py` (~L280, L311), `src/iai_mcp/cli/_import_sessions.py:185`.

**Source (reviewers + PRs):** #28 (gemini `_capture.py:311`; codex `_capture.py:280`), #30 (gemini `_import_sessions.py:185`, flagged CRITICAL).

issues.body:
**Impact:** The help text states `--store-path` defaults to `IAI_MCP_STORE` when set, but the argument defaults to `None` and the implementations fall back directly to `~/.iai-mcp` without consulting the env var. So operators who set `IAI_MCP_STORE` and omit `--store-path` silently operate on the wrong store. Affects the maintenance commands, `schema-cleanup` (`cmd_schema_cleanup`), and `sleep-cycle` (`cmd_maintenance_sleep_cycle`). Either honor the env var or fix the help.

issues.title: Correct the "read-only" labels - several commands mutate the store
issues.impact: Commands advertised/grouped as `[read-only]` actually write to the store: `recall` reinforces every hit (edges + `labile_until`); `audit drift` writes an `s5_drift_alert` event when the threshold is met; `session-start` writes a `session_started` event; `session refresh`/`session-refresh-if-stale` drains pending captures into the store; and the `lifecycle` group is labeled read-only but includes `force-unlock`, which removes the lockfile. issues.title: `README` import docs: `xargs --session-id`, `--max-turns`, drain-before-verify
issues.impact: Three doc bugs in the import recipes: (1) the `xargs` examples omit `--session-id`, so every imported transcript defaults to session `"-"`, collapsing all history under one session and breaking session filtering; (2) the documented backfill only queues the first 200 records because `capture-transcript` defaults `--max-turns` to 200 - needs a `--max-turns` note for >200-record transcripts; (3) `--no-spawn` only writes `.deferred-captures` files, so running `iai last` immediately after a backfill reports nothing until the deferred captures are drained.

issues.title: `add_subparsers(parser_class=...)` misuse (function where a class is expected; 3.11+)
issues.impact: `parser_class` in `add_subparsers` is a Python 3.11+ feature and expects a class, but `_raw_help_parser` is a function. On Python 3.10 it raises `TypeError: add_subparsers() got an unexpected keyword argument 'parser_class'`, and passing a function trips static type checkers. The project targets `>=3.11`, so the runtime risk is bounded, but the function-vs-class misuse should be fixed.
